LESSON: WRITING 9.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: APOLOGY LETTER

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.3: Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we write apology letters?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify key elements of an apology letter for comprehension
2. write an apology letter seeking reconciliation for effective communication
3. appreciate the use of letters in fostering peaceful co-existence in daily living

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 9.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: APOLOGY LETTER
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 9.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: APOLOGY LETTER
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify key elements of an apology letter for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to identify key elements of an apology letter for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify key elements of an apology letter for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify key elements of an apology letter for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write an apology letter seeking reconciliation for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to write an apology letter seeking reconciliation for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write an apology letter seeking reconciliation for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write an apology letter seeking reconciliation for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the use of letters in fostering peaceful co-existence in daily living

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the use of letters in fostering peaceful co-existence in daily living. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the use of letters in fostering peaceful co-existence in daily living.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the use of letters in fostering peaceful co-existence in daily living. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify key elements of an apology letter for comprehension)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter to a partner. (skill: write an apology letter seeking reconciliation for effective communication)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the use of letters in fostering peaceful co-existence in daily living)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify key elements of an apology letter for comprehension.
3. Practise this skill: write an apology letter seeking reconciliation for effective communication.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the use of letters in fostering peaceful co-existence in daily living.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we write apology letters?
2. what went well and why ● what did not go well and why?
3. what can be done differently next time?
4. what have they learnt?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify key elements of an apology letter for comprehension.
5. Be able to: write an apology letter seeking reconciliation for effective communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
